class.name: BulletFlock2D
class.brief_description: Makes bullets fly as a flock: they avoid each other, line up and stay grouped (boids).
class.description:
Makes bullets fly as a flock (boids): they keep their distance from each other, line up with their neighbors and stay grouped, while each bullet keeps its own speed. One resource holds one flock's rules. Every physics tick each bullet looks at its flockmates and turns its heading by a mix of three wishes, each with a strength in radians per second: - [member separation]: turn away from flockmates closer than [member separation_range] (personal space; this is what makes bullets avoid each other and re-order instead of overlapping). - [member alignment]: turn toward the average heading of the flockmates within [member neighbor_range] (makes the swarm fly the same way, like a school of fish). - [member cohesion]: turn toward the center of the flockmates within [member neighbor_range] (keeps the swarm together instead of drifting apart). [b]How to use it:[/b] on a [BulletSpawner2D], open the Flocking group and turn on [member BulletSpawner2D.flock_enabled]: that alone works, an empty [member BulletSpawner2D.flock] slot flies the default rules (the factory's [method BulletFactory2D.get_default_flock]). To tune, set [member BulletSpawner2D.flock] to a new BulletFlock2D and pick a [member preset] (Swarm, Fly Together, Keep Distance, Tight Group) as a starting point. Turn on homing too ([member BulletSpawner2D.homing_enabled]) and you see the swarm right away: the defaults are tuned for that, for any sprite size. For a volley you spawned from the factory, call [method BulletVolley2D.flock_join]: [codeblock] var swarm := BulletFlock2D.new() swarm.separation = 15.0 # stronger personal space than the default 10 swarm.separation_range = 40.0 # a 40 px gap between bullet edges $Spawner.flock = swarm $Spawner.flock_enabled = true
# Or for a factory volley: var volley: BulletVolley2D = $BulletFactory2D.spawn_volley(data) volley.flock_join(swarm) [/codeblock] [b]Bullet size is counted for you.[/b] With [member count_bullet_size] (the default) the ranges are gaps between bullet edges, so the same flock works for 16 px and 128 px bullets, scaled ones included. Turn it off only if you want plain center-to-center pixels. [b]Give the swarm a reason to stay together.[/b] Flocking only turns bullets, it never changes their speed. A pattern that explodes outward (a big ring or a wide triangle) carries the bullets out of each other's [member neighbor_range] within a second, and then there is nobody left to flock with. A swarm looks alive when the bullets share a goal: turn on homing ([member BulletSpawner2D.homing_enabled]) so they chase the target together while separation keeps them apart, or fire a tight pattern (fan, aimed, small ring). [b]Recipes[/b] (start here, then tune): - [i]Swarm chasing the player:[/i] the defaults with homing on. The swarm spreads while it closes in and buzzes around the target; the separation spreads the arrival (bullets queue around the target), so lower [member separation] to about 4 when every bullet should hit fast. - [i]Burst that fans out, then flocks:[/i] the defaults; [member blend_in_sec] lets the stacked shot open up for 0.3 s before the rules take over. Raise it to 0.6 for a longer fan. - [i]Orderly fish school:[/i] [code]alignment = 3, cohesion = 2[/code], the rest default. - [i]Bullets that only avoid each other[/i] (no grouping, no lining up): [code]alignment = 0, cohesion = 0[/code]. - [i]Tight ball that swirls:[/i] [code]cohesion = 5, alignment = 0.5, separation = 6, separation_range = 8[/code]. - [i]Wide, loose cloud:[/i] [code]separation_range = 80, neighbor_range = 300[/code]. - [i]Fair to dodge:[/i] [code]max_turn_rate_degrees = 120[/code] so no bullet can whip around faster than a third of a turn per second. - [i]Leader-and-follower streams:[/i] [code]view_angle_degrees = 180[/code] (bullets only follow what is ahead of them). [b]How a bullet turns:[/b] a bullet keeps its speed, so the mixed wish acts like a sideways force on a car: the heading turns at the wish's sideways part, in radians per second (a wish of 1 straight to the side turns the bullet one radian, about 57 degrees, per second). The part pointing straight back cannot turn a bullet, so a flockmate dead ahead turns it aside instead of around. A turn never passes the wish's direction and never exceeds [member max_turn_rate_degrees] (270 by default), so every turn is a smooth arc, even in a crowd or a burst stacked at the muzzle; it looks the same at any frame rate. Weights from 1 to 20 are typical (the inspector slider covers them; type a larger value if you need one). [b]Who flies together[/b] is decided where the flock is armed ([member BulletSpawner2D.flock_scope], or the scope of [method BulletVolley2D.flock_join]); separate flocks never see each other. Edits reach every bullet already in flight on the next tick ([code]swarm.cohesion = 2.0[/code]). Every accepted change emits [signal Resource.changed]; a rejected value pushes an error and keeps the old one. [b]Mixing with other features:[/b] homing turns first and the flock bends the result; a bullet crowded by a flockmate gives back its homing turn so it keeps its distance (see [member separation]). A spawner's homing turns at 5 radians per second by default ([member BulletSpawner2D.homing_smoothing]), which the default [member separation] of 10 outpaces; a homing that re-aims every tick ([member BulletVolleyData2D.homing_smoothing] 0) leaves the flock only a nudge. Wobble sways on top of the flock's heading; spin, bounce, graze, sound, pooling, random bullet sizes, texture rotation and time scale work as usual. A locked orbit owns the bullet's motion, and a direction curve in Override mode wins its axis. Frozen bullets are not flockmates, and nothing turns while the bullet world is frozen (time scale 0). [b]Limits:[/b] none hidden. The inspector sliders end at typical values but accept larger ones (type them in); a setter only refuses what has no meaning (negative or non-finite values, a [member neighbor_range] of 0, a [member view_angle_degrees] outside 0 to 360). [b]Cost:[/b] one pass per physics tick over every flocking bullet (an exact spatial hash grid), a few nanoseconds per flockmate looked at. [member max_neighbors] bounds the work per bullet and [member update_interval] spreads it over several ticks. Nothing is paid while no bullet flocks.

method.name: create_preset
method.description: Returns a new flock with the rules of [param preset] (see [enum Preset]; [constant PRESET_CUSTOM] returns the defaults). A bad id pushes an error and returns null. [codeblock] $Spawner.flock = BulletFlock2D.create_preset(BulletFlock2D.PRESET_FLY_TOGETHER) [/codeblock]

members.member: How strongly each bullet turns to fly the same way as its flockmates within [member neighbor_range] (per second). [b]Raise it[/b] (2 to 4) for an orderly school where everybody heads the same way; the swarm turns as one body. [b]Lower it[/b] toward 0 for a looser, messier swarm where bullets cross paths. 0 turns this rule off. Example: [code]alignment = 0[/code] together with [code]cohesion = 0[/code] keeps only the avoidance. Finite and >= 0.

How long a new volley's bullets take to ease into the flock, in seconds since the volley spawned (0 = full strength at once). The steering fades in smoothly (a smoothstep), so a burst stacked at the muzzle opens up in its pattern first and the flock takes over without a jolt; a volley reused from the pool eases in again. While a bullet eases in, it still counts as a flockmate, so older bullets make room for it. [b]Raise it[/b] (0.5 to 1) for patterns that should keep their shape a while before swarming; [b]lower it[/b] (0 to 0.1) for an instant reaction. Finite and >= 0.

How strongly each bullet turns toward the center of its flockmates within [member neighbor_range] (per second; it pulls harder the farther the center is, relative to the range). [b]Raise it[/b] (2 to 5) to keep the swarm in one tight blob that pulls stragglers back in; too high together with weak [member separation] makes bullets bunch up. [b]Lower it[/b] to let the swarm stretch and split into smaller groups. 0 turns this rule off. Finite and >= 0.

When on (the default), [member separation_range] and [member neighbor_range] are measured between bullet [b]edges[/b] instead of centers, so one setting fits every sprite: [code]separation_range = 24[/code] keeps a 24 px gap between 16 px bullets and between 128 px bullets alike, and bullets that overlap push harder than touching ones. A bullet's size is its drawn sprite ([member BulletVolleyData2D.texture_size], or the frame's size) times its own scale, so randomly scaled bullets keep their gaps too. Turn it off to measure plain center-to-center pixels (then size the ranges to your bullets yourself: [member separation_range] a bit more than one bullet's width). Costs about 10% more per flockmate check.

When on (the default), the bullet's sprite and collision shape turn with every flock turn, so arrows, fish and missiles always face where they fly ([member BulletVolleyData2D.texture_rotation_radians] is kept as the art's offset). Turn it off for round bullets, or when the sprite should keep its own rotation while the flight path bends. Rotation data that spins the bullet owns the sprite and is left alone either way. A rotation that drives the heading ([member BulletVolleyData2D.adjust_direction_based_on_rotation], or homing that steers through the rotation) still follows the flock, or the flock's turn would be undone.

How many flockmates each bullet reads per tick, nearest first (0 = no limit). Lower values make big, dense swarms cheaper and slightly looser; the visual difference above about 16 is small. Example: [code]max_neighbors = 8[/code] for thousands of bullets packed together. The scan start rotates per bullet, so a capped flock does not drift to one side. Real starlings track about 7. A stack of N bullets costs exactly N x max_neighbors distance checks.

The fastest the flock may turn a bullet, in degrees per second (0 = no cap). The default 270 keeps every turn a smooth arc, even inside a crowd or a burst stacked at the muzzle, while leaving the rules room to work. [b]Lower it[/b] to keep swarms fair to dodge: with [code]max_turn_rate_degrees = 120[/code] no bullet can reverse in less than 1.5 seconds, so the player can read the swarm; very low values (below about 45) make the rules too slow to matter. [b]Raise it[/b] (or 0) for twitchy, insect-like swarms. Homing and other steering are not capped by it.

How far a bullet sees its flockmates, in pixels: [member alignment] and [member cohesion] only consider flockmates closer than this. With [member count_bullet_size] (the default) it is the gap between the bullets' edges, so the default 150 works for any sprite size. [b]Larger[/b] (250 to 400) makes the whole swarm act as one big group (and costs a little more); [b]smaller[/b] (50 to 100) makes many small groups that ignore each other. If the bullets spread out farther than this, they stop flocking because nobody is in range. Finite and > 0.

The fastest way to a good swarm: pick a ready-made rule set in the inspector, then fine-tune. Picking one writes the steering knobs ([member separation], [member alignment], [member cohesion], both ranges, [member separation_lookahead_sec], [member max_turn_rate_degrees], [member blend_in_sec], [member view_angle_degrees]) and leaves [member count_bullet_size], [member face_heading], [member max_neighbors] and [member update_interval] alone. The menu shows the preset the current knobs match; it shows Custom as soon as you tune a knob off the preset, or when you pick Custom yourself (your values stay as they are and the menu stays on Custom until you pick a preset again). It is never saved (the knobs are). From code: [code]flock.apply_preset(BulletFlock2D.PRESET_KEEP_DISTANCE)[/code] (or [code]flock.preset = ...[/code]), [code]flock.get_preset()[/code] (what the menu shows), [code]flock.get_matching_preset()[/code] (the preset the values match), [method create_preset]. A bad id pushes an error and keeps the old values.

How fast each bullet turns away from flockmates inside [member separation_range] (radians per second at full push), and the rule that makes bullets keep their distance. Each flockmate pushes by [code]1 - gap / separation_range[/code] (touching: 1, overlapping: harder, at most 2). The bullet turns away from the side its flockmates are on, as hard as the geometric mean of its strongest single push and its average push: a crowd never dilutes the push to nothing, pushes from both sides still cancel, and a bullet buried in a stack pushes less than one at its edge, so a stack opens up like a fan. A bullet keeps its speed, so it steers [b]sideways[/b]: a flockmate dead ahead turns it aside, never around. [b]Separation outranks homing.[/b] A bullet touching or overlapping a flockmate gives back that share of its homing turn (all of it when overlapping) and steers away instead; once it has room, homing takes over again. So a homing swarm keeps its distance on the way and around the target instead of piling onto one point. [b]Raise it[/b] (15 to 20) for crisp personal space; [b]lower it[/b] (2 to 6) to let bullets brush past each other and reach a shared target sooner. 0 turns this rule (and its priority over homing) off. Finite and >= 0.

How far ahead [member separation] looks, in seconds: each pair is measured where both bullets will be after this time along their own flight (heading times speed), so flockmates already moving apart push less and flockmates about to collide push sooner. This damps the swerve: without it a crowd overcorrects and zigzags. 0 measures the pair where it is now. [b]Raise it[/b] (0.3 to 0.5) for fast bullets or a smoother, more anticipating swarm; [b]lower it[/b] for slow bullets that should only react to real contact. Finite and >= 0.

Personal space in pixels: flockmates closer than this push the bullet away (see [member separation]). With [member count_bullet_size] (the default) it is the gap between the bullets' edges: the default 24 keeps about a 24 px gap whatever the sprite size. With it off, it is the distance between centers, so set it a bit larger than one bullet's width. [b]Larger[/b] spreads the swarm out; [b]smaller[/b] packs it tight. It is independent of [member neighbor_range] and may even be larger. 0 turns separation off.

Turn inertia, in seconds: a bullet's turn rate eases toward what the rules ask over about this time, like a real bird that cannot reverse its wingbeat instantly. In a crowd the rules can ask for left, right, left from one tick to the next; with inertia the bullet sweeps smoothly instead of vibrating. 0 turns instantly. [b]Raise it[/b] (0.2 to 0.3) for heavier, lazier swarms; [b]lower it[/b] (0.03 to 0.05) for twitchy ones. Finite and >= 0.

Seconds between two steering updates of a bullet (0 = every physics tick, the default). Use it to make very large swarms cheaper: [code]update_interval = 3.0 / 60.0[/code] cuts the flock's cost to about a third with hardly a visible difference; values above about 0.2 s make the swarm react sluggishly. The updates are staggered across the flock so the work spreads evenly over the ticks; in between, every bullet keeps turning toward its last steering and still counts as a flockmate for the others. A bullet with no steering yet (a new or reused volley, a bullet woken from a freeze) computes at once, and any edit of this flock's rules makes every bullet compute anew on the next tick.

Field of view in degrees, centered on each bullet's flight heading: flockmates outside it are ignored by every rule (and do not count toward [member max_neighbors]). 360 (the default) sees all around. 180 sees only what is ahead, which turns a loose swarm into leader-and-follower streams (bullets follow the ones in front and ignore the ones behind). Narrow cones (below about 90) make bullets mostly ignore each other. Stacked flockmates (same position) are always seen so a stack still parts, and a bullet with no heading sees all around. Between 0 and 360.

constants.constant: The bullets of one spawner flock together, every shot of it included (a second wave merges into the first). For [method BulletVolley2D.flock_join] on a factory volley: the factory's own volleys of this flock.
Every spawner and volley using this resource with this scope is ONE flock: bullets of several enemies merge into one swarm.
Each volley (one shot) is its own flock: waves pass through each other without reacting.
Your own values (picking it changes nothing; the menu shows it once a knob differs from every preset).
The defaults: a swarm that spreads out while it chases its target and keeps clear gaps between bullets of any size. Start here for homing swarms.

One aligned ribbon, like a school of fish: strong [member alignment] (3) and [member cohesion] (2), a gentle [member separation] (6), a 180 deg/s turn cap. Good for streams that sweep across the screen.
Only avoid each other: [member alignment] and [member cohesion] 0, a wider personal space (32 px). Bullets keep their own paths and never overlap; ideal for bursts and random-size patterns.
Tight balls that swirl: strong [member cohesion] (5), a small personal space (8 px), a wide view (200 px). Good for blobs that orbit or roll toward the player.
